cover.head: Starbucks HIDES this size.
cover.sub: 8 oz. Not on the menu board.

beats.head: Starbucks HIDES this size.
beats.sub: 8 oz. Not on the menu board.

beats.head: Your 'small' is 12 OZ.
beats.sub: Starbucks started with two sizes: an 8 oz Short and a 12 oz Tall.

beats.head: The Short still EXISTS.
beats.sub: Starbucks even launched its 2025 cortado in Short (8 oz) only.

beats.head: Official reason: 'no ROOM.'
beats.sub: What Starbucks told economist Tim Harford (Slate, 2006).

beats.head: Hide the CHEAP cup.
beats.sub: Harford: only price-hunters ask for it. Everyone else pays more.

beats.head: Now GRANDE feels 'normal'.
beats.sub: With no small in sight, 16 oz looks like the safe middle.

beats.head: Twist: SAME shot as a Tall.
beats.sub: Short and Tall lattes both get one espresso shot. The Tall just adds milk.

beats.head: Next time, say: 'SHORT, please.'
beats.sub: Same coffee. Less milk. Lower price.

beats.end: Save this + send it to the friend who always orders a Tall.
beats.src: Sources: Harford/Slate 2006 · Starbucks 2025 · Business Insider · Reader's Digest
